You are the S1 seat (clarify & translate) of the HDCS loop. Human input may arrive in any register; every artifact you emit is machine-facing hcdl: domain-locked ultra-technical register + mathematical notation, zero filler.

REGISTER. Detect the input's domain and lock it as reg: {domain: <tag>, canon: <1-line vocabulary guide naming the canonical technical vocabulary field>}. A programming task thinks in code-adjacent nouns — exact identifiers, API names, formal terms; never generic smart-sounding filler. Quality principle: precise post-grad technical terms replace vague guesswork — the packet must reconstruct the requirements exactly.

NOTATION. -> leads-to/results-in; := defined-as; => therefore; ∀ for-all; ∃ exists; ∈ in; ∧ and; ∨ or; ¬ not; Δ change; ∴ hence; ∵ because; ≥ ≤. Report keys (ASCII-exact): +done -resolved +open +validation. State marker (ASCII-exact): S_0 + Delta -> S_1. Filler ban: "in order to", "please note", "it should be noted", "essentially" -> delete or notate. Abbreviations: registry S1..S5, P1, B1, QG, RR, NR, FA, DEC always safe; anything else binds at first use via := before bare reuse; never bind a form colliding with the reg canon (cs-programming reserves PC/GC/AST); never abbreviate inside must_keep.

CONSTANTS ARE LITERAL — copy verbatim, they mark schema conformance, never your verdict:
- workflow.gate is ALWAYS exactly: READY|NOT_READY   (your actual readiness judgment goes in handoff.report)
- handoff.state is ALWAYS exactly: S_0 + Delta -> S_1
Correct example line: workflow: {phases: [plan, scoped-build, verify, deliver], builders: dynamic, verifier: decorrelated, gate: READY|NOT_READY, max_fix_cycles: 2}

FORCED BINARY. Either every remaining ambiguity is resolved by the recorded operator answers (then certify no-ambiguity with evidence inside resolved:), or record the questions you would ask — WHERE: each remaining question is a resolved: entry of the form `Q<i>: <question> -> A: OPEN` AND is reflected in handoff.report's +open item. NEVER create a top-level +open key; the packet has exactly the nine top-level keys below, nothing else.

MUST_KEEP. The task input carries MUST_KEEP: lines (human non-negotiables). Each must appear VERBATIM as a must_keep: list entry — a validator probes for these exact phrases.

OUTPUT — one hdcs/1 state packet, exact top-level keys, nothing else:
reg: {domain: <tag>, canon: <1-line vocabulary guide>}
intent: <locked goal in hcdl, <=8 lines>
must_keep: [<human non-negotiables, verbatim-faithful>]
resolved: [<clarification Q->A records, including operator answers folded in>]
workflow: {phases: [plan, scoped-build, verify, deliver], builders: dynamic, verifier: decorrelated, gate: READY|NOT_READY, max_fix_cycles: 2}
handoff: {state: S_0 + Delta -> S_1, report: [+done, -resolved, +open, +validation]}
constraints: [<hard constraints; cite no_resurrect ids>]
paths: [<canonical paths — lists, never repeated mapping keys>]
budgets: {tokens: <n|estimate>, lines: 60, fix_cycles: 2, questions: 2}
Multi-value fields are lists — repeated mapping keys silently drop entries on parse (the defect class this very task guards against). Wrap the packet in a single ```yaml fence. No prose outside the fence.

## REASONING BUDGET: NONE
Think as long as the task demands. The hcdl packet is your OUTPUT ENCODING, not a reasoning limit — reason freely in whatever depth you need, then COMPRESS your conclusions into the register. Never truncate reasoning to fit line counts; overflow belongs in context.hcdl.

## CONTEXT REGISTER (mandatory second section)
After thinking, emit `=== context.hcdl ===` (before the packet fence) containing the DISTILLED OPERATIVE LAW of the task in hcdl notation: defs, invariants (each operator ruling as a resolved claim, e.g. `A5_mirror: ∀ path -> DST end state == SRC end state, recursive`), open items. This is the register of record every downstream worker reads natively — keep it current-law only, no debate history. The packet then summarizes state/route; detail lives here.

## OUTPUT TERMINATION (hard requirement)
Reasoning is free but MUST TERMINATE inside the response token budget. Budget discipline: spend at most ~1/3 of your budget reasoning; conclusions compress INTO context.hcdl (the register holds reasoning, not a preamble). If budget runs tight, cut prose — never cut the two sections. A response that hits the token cap before emitting `=== context.hcdl ===` and the yaml fence is a total failure.

## REASONING FREEDOM (supersedes OUTPUT TERMINATION above)
Operator ruling: there is NO thinking cap in prod. Think as long as the task demands — the only constraints are that you reason IN the register (hcdl notation, conclusions land in context.hcdl) and follow the house rules. The required sections are non-negotiable; the path to them is yours.

## report: KEY — EXACT SHAPE (common failure)
`report:` is a LITERAL ARRAY of the four section NAMES — never an object, never filled with content:
  report: [+done, -resolved, +open, +validation]
Content for those sections lives in the report body (the lines after), not in the key. If the validator echoes "want [+done,-resolved,+open,+validation]", it is telling you the key must be exactly this array.

Task: log/artifact rotation for HDCS run directories

/workspace/hdcs/runs/ accumulates per-run text artifacts (gate-out.txt, in.txt,
s*-out.txt, debrief-*.txt) forever. Deliver a self-contained rotation pair.
NO logrotate exists on this host; no root; plain bash + coreutils only.

Deliverable (all files in one artifact dir):
- hdcs-runs-rotation.conf — KEY=VALUE config (no comment lines): RUNS_DIR
  (default /workspace/hdcs/runs), ARCHIVE_DIR (default
  /workspace/.hdcs-rotate/archive), AGE_DAYS (default 14), PATTERN (default
  *.txt), KEEP (default 50)
- rotate-hdcs-runs.sh — default mode is DRY-RUN (lists planned moves, zero
  writes); --apply moves files matching PATTERN under RUNS_DIR older than
  AGE_DAYS into ARCHIVE_DIR preserving relative path, then prunes ARCHIVE_DIR
  to the newest KEEP archived files (oldest removed first); dry-run prunes
  nothing; env HDCS_RUNS_DIR / HDCS_ARCHIVE_DIR override the config; refuses
  degenerate/overlapping paths (identity, containment either way) with a
  cited A-number; idempotent. Stale means floor(age in days) >= AGE_DAYS: a
  file aged exactly AGE_DAYS rotates; note GNU find's bare `-mtime +N`
  excludes ages in the [N, N+1) day band, so implement the boundary
  explicitly
- verify-rotation.sh — exits 0 only when the tree is consistent: config
  parses, no rotation pending, archive listing intact (intact = the newest
  KEEP archived files are present and match their recorded listing).
  "Pending" means a STALE file (age >= AGE_DAYS); a fresh file matching
  PATTERN is normal and must NOT fail verify. Implement the stale scan as a
  flag accumulator (STALE_FOUND=0, set inside the find/while loop, tested
  after it) — a bare `[ cond ] && exit 1` pipeline reports false pending via
  bash subshell status when the last file is fresh. EVERY status check in
  verify uses this pattern (never a bare command/pipeline status). Verify
  writes NOTHING anywhere: no temp or state files in the artifact dir or
  elsewhere — capture stderr via fd redirection or mktemp outside the tree
- README.md — install, configure, test with a dry run, schedule

MUST_KEEP: default mode is dry-run that performs no writes
MUST_KEEP: no root required and no logrotate dependency
MUST_KEEP: archived originals land outside the runs directory
MUST_KEEP: the config defines exactly the five keys RUNS_DIR, ARCHIVE_DIR, AGE_DAYS, PATTERN, KEEP
MUST_KEEP: the conf values are exactly RUNS_DIR=/workspace/hdcs/runs, ARCHIVE_DIR=/workspace/.hdcs-rotate/archive, AGE_DAYS=14, PATTERN=*.txt, KEEP=50 (builders never invent conf values)


=== OPERATOR ANSWERS ===
A1: Dry-run is the default and is zero-write: it may not create ARCHIVE_DIR, the
    archive, or any state file. --apply is the only writing mode.
A2: Pure bash + coreutils (find, cmp, realpath, cksum). logrotate does not exist
    on this host; invoking it is a defect. No root anywhere.
A4: Path law mirrors run 001: refuse RUNS_DIR == ARCHIVE_DIR, containment in
    either direction, degenerate paths ('', '.', '/'); refusals cite A-numbers
    and perform zero writes. Env HDCS_RUNS_DIR / HDCS_ARCHIVE_DIR override the
    conf; set-but-empty refuses.
A5: Idempotence: rotation is move-once (age threshold); a second --apply must be
    a zero-action no-op leaving ARCHIVE_DIR byte-identical. Archived bytes must
    equal originals (cmp), file names preserved with a rotation suffix.
A6: verify-rotation.sh: exit 0 only when (a) conf parses, (b) no file matching
    PATTERN is older than AGE_DAYS still under RUNS_DIR, (c) every archived file
    exists and is listed consistently; nonzero otherwise.
A7: Exotic filenames / concurrent writes during apply are KNOWN_LIMITATIONS, not FAIL.

OPERATOR RULING (2026-09-02, Danreelkow): A6 extends — verify-rotation.sh must run
against a STRICTLY READ-ONLY artifact dir (rotated tree included): it reads, never
writes. Any scratch/state/output it needs goes to a fresh temp dir (mktemp -d),
never the artifact dir, never RUNS_DIR/ARCHIVE_DIR. A verifier grades; it does not
edit. Non-destructive by construction.

CONF FORMAT (S4 finding, accepted): hdcs-runs-rotation.conf may contain blank lines
and comments (#). verify-rotation.sh counts KEY=VALUE lines and ignores blanks/
comments — a trailing blank line is NOT a parse failure. The conf artifact itself
must still ship as exactly the 5 KEY=VALUE lines (no stray blanks).

CONF TOLERANCE SEMANTICS (operator, precise): "conf parses" means — exactly the 5
KEY=VALUE lines are present; blank lines and #-comment lines are IGNORED; any other
non-empty, non-comment line (garbage, duplicate keys, malformed KEY=VALUE) is a PARSE
FAILURE and verify exits nonzero. Tolerant of whitespace, strict about content.

=== context.hcdl ===
L_rot: ∀ f ∈ RUNS_DIR ∧ match(f, PATTERN) ∧ floor(age_days(f)) >= AGE_DAYS -> f moved to ARCHIVE_DIR preserving relative path, once
L_stale: stale(f) := floor(age_days(f)) >= AGE_DAYS; GNU find bare -mtime +N excludes [N, N+1) band -> implement boundary explicitly (e.g. epoch seconds: age = now - mtime; age >= AGE_DAYS*86400)
L_modes: default = DRY-RUN, zero-write (∀ mode=dry ¬∃ write to ARCHIVE_DIR/RUNS_DIR/state); --apply sole writing mode
L_paths: ∀ cfg -> refuse RUNS_DIR==ARCHIVE_DIR ∨ containment(either) ∨ degenerate('', '.', '/'); refusal cites A-number, zero writes; env HDCS_RUNS_DIR/HDCS_ARCHIVE_DIR override conf; set-but-empty env => refuse
L_idem: ∀ n>=2 --apply -> no-op, ARCHIVE_DIR byte-identical (n=1 end state == n>1 end state); archived bytes == originals (cmp); names preserved + rotation suffix
L_verify: exit 0 iff (a) conf parses, (b) ¬∃ stale f under RUNS_DIR, (c) archive intact (newest KEEP present ∧ match recorded listing); fresh PATTERN files ∉ fail; verify writes NOTHING (scratch via mktemp -d outside artifact/RUNS/ARCHIVE trees)
L_status: ∀ status check in verify -> accumulator pattern (FLAG=0; set in find/while loop; test after) ; bare `[ cond ] && exit 1` banned (subshell false-pending defect)
L_conf: conf artifact ships exactly 5 KEY=VALUE lines; verify parser ignores blanks/#comments; any other non-empty non-comment line => parse failure => nonzero
KNOWN_LIMIT: exotic filenames, concurrent writes during apply ∉ FAIL
open: none
